title: The West Bengal Teacher Recruitment Scam
dek: A state's teacher-hiring exams were allegedly rigged for cash. Investigators recovered so much physical currency from one associate's flats that it had to be counted with note-counting machines running for days.

heroStat.label: in cash alone recovered from one associate's properties

promise.quote: Teacher recruitment through the West Bengal School Service Commission (SSC) will be conducted on merit, through fair and transparent examinations.
promise.madeBy: West Bengal School Service Commission, under the state's School Education Department
promise.role: State body responsible for recruiting teachers to government and government-aided schools
promise.context: Allegations centred on recruitment exams held in preceding years, with investigators alleging candidates paid bribes, routed through officials and intermediaries, to secure teaching posts they had not qualified for on merit.

target.description: Recruitment based strictly on exam merit, with no manipulation of results, waitlists, or appointment orders in exchange for payment.
target.standard: Standard public recruitment norms requiring merit-based selection through the Commission's own examination process.

reality.description: The Enforcement Directorate arrested then-Education Minister Partha Chatterjee in July 2022 and, in raids on properties linked to his associate Arpita Mukherjee, recovered cash in stages reported at ₹20 crore, then ₹15 crore, then ₹27.9 crore, with an earlier search separately reported at ₹49.8 crore in cash and jewellery worth ₹5.08 crore — among the largest cash seizures in an Indian corruption investigation. The ED separately said it had attached assets worth ₹641 crore linked to the case. Chatterjee was granted conditional bail by the Supreme Court in early 2025 after roughly three years in custody.

gap.metricLabel: Assets the ED says it has attached vs. cash physically recovered in raids
gap.actualDisplay: ₹49.8 cr in cash recovered in one set of raids
gap.note: Reported cash-recovery figures vary across different raids and reports (₹15 cr, ₹20 cr, ₹27.9 cr, and ₹49.8 cr all appear in different accounts); this investigation has not fully reconciled these into a single total and reports the largest single figure found.

timeline.label: Major cash seizures begin
timeline.detail: Raids on properties linked to Arpita Mukherjee recover tens of crores in cash and gold over several days.

keyIndividuals.name: Partha Chatterjee
keyIndividuals.outcome: Arrested July 2022; granted conditional bail by the Supreme Court, early 2025, after roughly three years in custody. No trial verdict confirmed as of the sources reviewed.

keyIndividuals.name: Arpita Mukherjee
keyIndividuals.outcome: Properties linked to her were the site of the case's largest cash recoveries. This investigation has not confirmed her current legal status.

verdict.summary: Preliminary verdict, pending fuller research: the scale of cash recovered from properties linked to the case is extraordinary and well documented by multiple independent reports of the raids themselves. This investigation has not yet established the trial's current stage or confirmed any verdict for either principal accused.
verdict.reasoning: This entry was added to establish the case's place in the site's timeline and its headline facts, which are strongly corroborated by physical evidence (recovered cash) reported across multiple sources. Confidence in the overall case status is capped at low because this investigation has not yet traced the case to a confirmed trial verdict.
